data.title: US SEC's Nvidia probe is examining potential accounting issues, sources say
data.description:
By Chris Prentice and Alexandra Alper

The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip giant.

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at the company.

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.

Still, the accounting focus of the probe, which Reuters is reporting for the first time, increases pressure on Nvidia, whose investors are still reeling from revelations about ousted CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital relationships, including with Alice Huang, who US authorities suspect is a Chinese spy. China has denied she is a spy.

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week.

The crisis has sent shares in Nvidia, a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing.

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted "lawful business." Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The SEC probe is the latest of Nvidia's legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported last month.

data.title: YouTube nears $3B settlement in social media addiction lawsuit brought by school districts -- Bloomberg
data.description:
Google’s YouTube is nearing a settlement with school districts across the U.S. over claims that the platform has harmed the mental health of students with a purposely built design that encourages endless scrolling, autoplay videos, and algorithm-driven recommendations that create addictive feeds.

According to sources cited by Bloomberg, the ~$3B settlement aims to reimburse the plaintiffs for “institutional costs of social media addiction,” specifically mental health counseling to address depression, anxiety, eating disorders, and suicide. Sources say YouTube and the school districts have agreed to a settlement “in principle” with additional conditions to include product safeguards.

The lawsuit accuses sites like YouTube of knowing the risks of compulsive social media use but failing to design features to prevent addiction. The lawsuit was particularly problematic for YouTube and its parent company Google, given the proliferation of Chromebook laptops among students and teachers’ use of instructional YouTube videos.

The proposed agreement between YouTube and school districts settles just one of thousands of lawsuits against Google’s YouTube and other social media sites like Facebook , Instagram , Snap , and TikTok (TIKTOK).

In February, YouTube , Meta , Snap and TikTok (TIKTOK) will face a California judge who will rule on a lawsuit from the Tucson (AZ) Unified School District as part of the federal multidistrict litigation.

data.title: Columbia Seligman Premium Technology Growth Fund Announces a Special Fourth Quarter Distribution
data.description:
Today, Columbia Seligman Premium Technology Growth Fund, Inc. () (the Fund) declared a special fourth quarter distribution, that is beyond its typical quarterly managed distribution policy, in the amount of $13.2298 per share. A federal excise tax of 4% applies to funds that do not distribute substantially all of their annual income (including net gains) before the end of their fiscal year. The Fund’s income for the 2026 fiscal year exceeds the amounts previously distributed pursuant to the Fund’s quarterly managed distribution policy. The Fund is distributing this excess income so that it will not incur the 4% federal excise tax in 2026.

The distribution will be paid on December 22, 2026 (the Payment Date) to stockholders of record on December 2, 2026 (the Record Date). The ex-dividend date is December 23, 2026. Because all of the distribution is expected to be a special capital gain distribution, it will automatically be paid in stock except that any Record Date stockholder may elect to receive the distribution in cash by contacting, as applicable, their financial advisor (for shareholders who hold shares through a financial intermediary, such as a broker-dealer) or the Fund’s stockholder servicing agent, Equiniti Trust Company, LLC, whose contact information appears below (for shareholders who hold shares directly with the Fund), by 5 pm Eastern Time on December 16, 2026. It is anticipated that the Fund will make its next distribution under its managed distribution policy in the month of February.

Because the payment of the special dividend represents more than 25% of the market price per share of the Company’s common shares, the New York Stock Exchange has advised the Company that its common shares will trade with “due bills” representing an assignment of the right to receive the special dividend from the record date of December 2, 2026 through the closing of trading on NYSE on December 22, 2026, which is the payment date and the last day of trading before the December 23, 2026 ex-dividend date (this period of time representing the “Dividend Right Period”).

Shareholders who sell their common shares during the Dividend Right Period will be selling their right to the special dividend, and such shareholders will not be entitled to receive the special dividend. Due bills obligate a seller of common shares to deliver the special dividend payable on such common shares to the buyer (the “Dividend Right”). The record date of December 2, 2026 will be used as the date for establishing the due bill tracking of the Dividend Right to the holder of common shares.

Due bill obligations are customarily settled between the brokers representing the buyers and the sellers of shares. The Company has no obligation for either the amount of the due bill or the processing of the due bill. Buyers and sellers of the Company’s common shares should consult their brokers before trading to be sure they understand the effect of NYSE’s due bill procedures.

data.title: Bitcoin drops 7% to its lowest level since July as crypto sell-off deepens
data.description:
Bitcoin fell more than 7% on Friday afternoon, November 20, 2026. Intraday lows landed somewhere between $59,000 and $61,300, the weakest levels the asset has seen since early July.

At the start of November, Bitcoin was trading above $81,000. Three weeks later, the people who bought that top would probably prefer not to check their portfolios.

The drop did not happen in isolation. Ether and Solana also slid as the wider digital asset market turned decisively negative, and the selling spilled well beyond crypto into equities.

Bitcoin's November losses now sit at approximately 20% to 23% from its start-of-month highs. That puts the month on track to be Bitcoin's worst since June 2022.

Leverage made the slide sharper. More than $700 million in leveraged positions were wiped out in the 24 hours leading up to November 20, and most of them were long bets on prices going up.

Institutional money was heading for the exits as well. Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582 million in net outflows on November 19, the biggest single-day withdrawal in several weeks.

Forbes described Friday's move as the continuation of a heavy tumble from the highs Bitcoin reached over the summer. The early November peak near $81,000 turned out to be a brief rally rather than the start of a new leg up.

Before Friday's break, Bitcoin had been holding a range of roughly $62,000 to $64,000. It had struggled to keep any gains after that early November peak, and the range finally gave way.

The macro backdrop did crypto no favors. The downturn has been tied to fading momentum in technology and AI-related stocks, with the high-profile IPO of Anthropic linked to a rotation of capital across risk assets.

Rising Treasury yields added pressure. So did speculation about a potential interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve in December.

The sell-off reached Asian markets too. South Korea's KOSPI index fell roughly 5%, a drop steep enough to trigger trading halts.

The immediate focus is the $60,000 level. Round numbers carry outsized psychological weight in markets, and this one now sits right at the edge of Friday's trading range.

Leveraged traders often cluster their stop-losses and liquidation thresholds around obvious levels like this. If Bitcoin breaks decisively below $60,000, that could set off another wave of forced selling, adding volatility to an already fragile market.

There is also a cost-basis question. The recent selling pressure may indicate that the average Bitcoin holder is getting close to breakeven, which tends to be a moment when conviction gets tested.

The ETF data deserves close attention in the coming sessions. A $582 million single-day outflow suggests institutional appetite is cooling as macro uncertainty builds, and continued redemptions from Bitcoin products would remove a key source of demand.

data.title: Why Bausch + Lomb shares are getting obliterated today
data.description:
What happened?

Shares of eyecare company Bausch + Lomb fell 5% in the afternoon session after the company's study of BL1332 did not show a statistically significant improvement on its primary 24-hour pain-relief endpoint.

According to a company press release, the study did not meet its primary endpoint of demonstrating a statistically significant improvement versus vehicle in the sum of pain intensity differences (SPID) over 24 hours. The release showed a least-squares mean difference versus vehicle of -11.5 for BL1332 0.30% and -9.0 for BL1332 0.15%, with negative values favoring BL1332 indicating greater pain relief.

Shares may have fallen because failing to reach statistical significance on that measure weakened the evidence of efficacy for BL1332 and left its next development steps uncertain.

After the initial drop, the shares shed some of the losses and rose to $19.75, down 4.5% from the previous close.

What is the market telling us

Bausch + Lomb’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 3 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 23 days ago when the stock gained 8.7% on the news that the company reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $1.375 billion and raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance. According to a company press release, Bausch + Lomb reported total revenue of $1.375 billion, up 7% compared to the prior-year period, with constant currency revenue rising 8% across its vision care, pharmaceutical, and surgical divisions. Adjusted earnings per share was 34 cents, up from 18 cents in the same quarter last year and above analysts' consensus estimates of 22 cents. Adjusted EBITDA was $325 million, above analyst estimates of $270.9 million.

For the full year, the company lifted its revenue guidance to $5.5 billion at the midpoint from $5.49 billion. Full-year EBITDA guidance of $1.12 billion at the midpoint was also above analyst estimates of $1.05 billion.

data.title: Gold Nosedives As Expectations For Fed Rate Hike Continue To Increase
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Gold prices have gone into freefall on Friday as more U.S. Federal Reserve bankers join the list of officials voicing support for raising interest rates in December to combat inflation. Concerns over potential high U.S. interest rates weighed against gold, with traders pricing in a quarter-point rate hike as a certainty.

Front Month Comex Gold for December delivery has gone for a tailspin by $164.20 (or 4.46%) to $3,521.30 per troy ounce.

Front Month Comex Silver for December delivery has also nosedived by $3.319 (or 7.48%) to $41.040 per troy ounce.

Yesterday, in a speech before the Money Marketeers of New York University, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson emphasized that inflation needs to be the policy priority as the labor market is at full employment.

Paulson stressed that the way to bring down inflation is by raising rates though she advocated adopting a step-by-step increase rather than a drastic move to allow time for the economy to adjust to higher costs.

Earlier, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee stated that he would consider all options available to counter stubborn U.S. inflation.

Over the past few days, several other senior Fed officials have expressed support for a rate hike.

The Federal Open Market Committee is slated to hold its next meeting on December 8-9.

According to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, investors are currently betting on a 93.80% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate-hike at the upcoming meeting. The odds on the rates being held at the current level stand at 6.20%.

On Wednesday, the minutes of the FOMC's October meeting were released. Notably, the report stated that almost all participants were in agreement that a rate hike would be appropriate to bring inflation to the 2.00% objective.

The committee had voted 10-2 last month to hold the benchmark federal funds rate in the 3.75% to 4.00% range, while Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented and wanted a quarter-percentage point hike.

Hours before the release of the minutes, Fed Governor Christopher Waller stated that the Fed needs to 'shock people' with a half-percentage-point increase in the coming meeting.

Days before, the New York Times reported that U.S. President Donald Trump is considering a renewal of strikes on Iran, joining hands with Israel.

Trump too remarked that he had reports indicating that Iran is possibly developing chemical or biological weapons after the U.S. disabled its nuclear weapon capabilities.

However, bringing relief to markets, Trump suggested putting off major decisions on Iran until 2027. The significance of the date is unclear as yet.

While on his way back to the U.S. after attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, in an interview with Reuters, Trump stated that the Iran matter can be discussed after the New Year begins.

In an interview with Fox News, which was aired yesterday, Trump remarked that he preferred to see what happens after January 1.

In a telephone interview with Axios, Trump stated that he was not rushing on any decision on Iran.

Similarly, in an interview with News 12, Trump repeated that he is not rushing to make any decisions until after the new year starts.

Yesterday, in the U.S. Congress, the Senate rejected (in a 48 to 51 vote) a resolution by the House of Representatives intended to rein in Trump's powers to order strikes on Iran.

Today, the WTI crude oil for December was last seen trading, down by $0.09 (or 0.11%), at $83.30 per barrel.

Largely unchanged, the U.S. Dollar Index was last seen trading at 103.82, down by 0.07 (or 0.07%).

data.title: Simmons Bank Issues Statement Correcting Inaccurate Media Reports Regarding Texas Multifamily Project
data.description:
PINE BLUFF, Ark., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Simmons Bank (Simmons or Bank), a wholly owned subsidiary of Simmons First National Corporation (), today issued the following statement regarding inaccurate information contained in recent articles concerning a loan to a real estate developer to finance a Texas multifamily project (Project):

Recent media reports regarding this Project contain inaccuracies. Most notably, the loan balance stated in the reports of $133 million is incorrect. The total financing provided by Simmons with respect to the Project was approximately $88 million, of which approximately $44 million was participated to another financial institution, and all of which is secured by a first lien on the property serving as collateral. Based on recent appraisals, the value of the property that serves as collateral to the loan remains well in excess of the outstanding loan balance, with an approximate loan-to-value ratio of 73 percent, and the Bank does not currently expect to incur a credit loss related to the Project.

The foreclosure filing referenced in the media reports is part of the bank's standard strategy for protecting its interests while continuing to pursue a resolution. Simmons remains engaged in constructive discussions with the Project sponsors regarding a potential workout strategy.

Simmons Bank Simmons Bank is a wholly owned subsidiary of Simmons First National Corporation (), a Mid-South based financial holding company that has paid cash dividends to its shareholders for 117 consecutive years. Its principal subsidiary, Simmons Bank, operates 220 branches in Arkansas, Kansas, Missouri, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas. Founded in 1903, Simmons Bank offers comprehensive financial solutions delivered with a client-centric approach. Recently, Simmons Bank was recognized by Newsweek as one of America's Best Regional Banks and Credit Unions 2026, by Forbes as one of America's Best-In-State Companies 2026 and by American Banker as one of the Top Performing Banks 2026 with $10 billion to $50 billion of assets. data.title: Trump Says He'd Love to See Jensen Huang Back at Nvidia — WSJ
data.description:
By WSJ Staff

President Trump, taking questions from reporters at the White House Friday, said Nvidia's CEO search should include a very familiar name: Jensen Huang.

"I think there are very few people at that company that could do" what Huang, the former CEO, did, Trump said. "He put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies."

Huang resigned earlier this month after a scandal involving extramarital affairs with with a suspected Chinese spy and an employee.

"We have to protect our brilliant people. Jensen is one of them," Trump added. "I think the company if they were smart they'd take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work."

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Union Pacific engineers' union wins nearly $100 million for schedule rule violation
data.description:
A union representing locomotive engineers at railroad operator Union Pacific has won a $98.8 million payout over a contract violation, the International Brotherhood of Teamsters said on Friday.

The Special Board of Adjustment, an arbitration tribunal, ruled that Union Pacific failed to implement a new work rule meant to ensure consistent scheduling, negotiated by its locomotive engineers' union in 2023, Teamsters said.

  • In 2023, the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen (BLET) of the Teamsters Rail Conference negotiated an "11/4" schedule of 11 working days followed by 4 days off

  • The union said the company did not implement the policy within the mandated deadline, nor did it request an extension

  • The tribunal directed Union Pacific to pay each claimant one basic day's pay, based on their applicable assignment, for every calendar day they claimed during the period when the 11/4 benefit was denied

  • The period during which the benefit was denied ran from June 30, 2024, to January 27, 2025

  • Union Pacific is required to calculate the final payments owed within 30 days, Teamsters said

  • The company did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment
